text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.

- Die Erste savings bank is planning a consortium with an Austrian insurer and a strategical foreign partner to take over 70 percent of government's stake in Creditanstalt. It is searching for a partner to buy the remainder and will hold talks with EA-Generali.
- Finance Minister Viktor Klima wants to get the privatisation of Creditanstalt over and done with by the end of this year.
- Textile industry to see more job losses in the near future, even though turnover increased this year.
- Austria has lost its commanding position in high quality exports to the Czech Republic.

- Education Minister Elisabeth Gehrer to become Austria's first woman president and chancellor today when she stands in for hospitalised President Thomas Klestil, and Chancellor Franz Vranitzky and Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel, who are both abroad.
- Parliamentary president Heinz Fischer believes a referendum over possible abolition of Austria's neutrality is a must.
- CA-chief Guido Schmidt-Chiari expects speedy privatisation of the bank. He would like to have a German partner.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV wants to financially participate with Austria's provincial electricity distributors.
- Austria's net income will fall in 1997 as inflation and federal spending cuts take effect dampen pay rises.
- OMV is planning to search for oil in Libya and Algeria together with a partner.

- Food maker Mautner-Markhof Nahrungs- und Genumittel Beteilgungs AG reported an operating loss of 54 million schillings for the first half of 1996 compared to a loss of eight million the year before.
- The new tender for Creditanstalt is expected in two weeks.
